Question: How should layered/multilayered Zirconia, Esthetic Zirconia, Porcelain/Ceramic Zirconia, and multiple shades on the Rx be handled?
Official Answer / SOP: If the Rx notes contain the wording 'layered zirconia' or 'multilayered zirconia,' escalate the case to Orange County (OC). Multilayered Zirconia had previously been clarified as PFZ-related for this workflow, so it should not be processed as a normal Zirconia case. If the Rx says 'Esthetic Zirconia,' proceed with entry because it is treated as regular Zirconia. If the material is written as Porcelain/Ceramic Zirconia, proceed with case entry unless another separate escalation rule applies. If the Rx contains more than one shade, include all shades listed in the Rx notes.
Keywords: layered zirconia, multilayered zirconia, multilayer zirconia, PFZ, esthetic zirconia, aesthetic zirconia, regular zirconia, Porcelain Ceramic Zirconia, porcelain/ceramic zirconia, multiple shades, more than one shade, two shades, Rx notes, escalate OC, proceed
Notes: Rx-specific material and shade rules. Layered or multilayered Zirconia requires OC escalation. Esthetic Zirconia is treated as regular Zirconia and may proceed. Porcelain/Ceramic Zirconia may proceed unless another confirmed escalation condition applies.
Source Basis: Current team process clarifications provided September-October 2026
Purpose: Define how to handle specific Zirconia wording and multiple shade instructions found in Rx notes.
Step-by-Step Procedure:
1. Review the Rx notes and material wording before continuing case entry.
2. If the Rx notes say 'layered zirconia' or 'multilayered zirconia,' stop normal entry and escalate the case to Orange County (OC).
3. If the Rx says 'Esthetic Zirconia,' proceed with entry as regular Zirconia unless another independent escalation condition is present.
4. If the Rx says Porcelain/Ceramic Zirconia, proceed with case entry unless another independent escalation condition is present.
5. Review every shade listed in the Rx notes.
6. If more than one shade is listed, enter/include all shades exactly as instructed on the Rx rather than selecting only one.
7. Continue the normal case-entry and QC process after applying the correct material and shade rule.
Stop / Escalate When: Always escalate to OC when 'layered zirconia' or 'multilayered zirconia' appears in the Rx notes. Escalate any material description that remains unclear or conflicts with another confirmed routing rule.
Title: Rx Zirconia Material & Multiple-Shade Handling
Search Intent Examples: The Rx says layered zirconia. Can I enter it? The Rx says multilayered zirconia. Should I escalate? Is multilayered zirconia PFZ? The Rx says Esthetic Zirconia. Can I proceed? Question: How should multiple Rx files or an additional scan for the same patient be handled?
Official Answer / SOP: When the same patient has two Rx files and the second Rx/scan is an additional scan for that same case, upload both Rx files together under the same ABS case. If the second scan specifically states 'to add' or 'need under partial,' add that scan under Partial instead of combining it with the normal Rx upload.
Keywords: two Rx, 2 Rx, multiple Rx, additional scan, same patient, upload together, partial, to add, need under partial, Cynthia Smart
Notes: Example provided: Cynthia Smart. First Rx is the Rx used for ABS entry and may note that an additional scan will be uploaded; the second Rx/scan is the additional scan for the same patient. Upload them together unless the second scan explicitly says 'to add' or 'need under partial.'
Purpose: Define how to attach multiple Rx/additional scans for the same patient and when an additional scan must be placed under Partial.
Step-by-Step Procedure:
1. Confirm that both Rx files/scans belong to the same patient and the same case.
2. Review the first Rx and its notes for any statement that an additional scan will be uploaded.
3. Review the second Rx/scan and confirm that it is the additional scan for the same patient/case.
4. If the second Rx/scan is simply the additional scan for the same case, upload both Rx files together under the same ABS case.
5. If the second scan specifically states 'to add' or 'need under partial,' add that scan under Partial instead of treating it as the normal combined Rx upload.
6. Verify that all required files are attached to the correct patient/case before completion.
Stop / Escalate When: Stop and verify if the two Rx files/scans do not clearly belong to the same patient/case, if the second scan instructions are unclear, or if you cannot determine whether it belongs under Partial.
Title: Multiple Rx / Additional Scan Upload Handling
Search Intent Examples: The patient has two Rx files. Do I upload both? There is an additional scan for the same patient. Where do I upload it? The second scan says to add under partial. What do I do? Need under partial. Cynthia Smart additional scan.

Question: How should a single-unit Zirconia Monolithic Inlay/Onlay case be handled?
Official Answer / SOP: If the Rx is for a single-unit Zirconia Monolithic Inlay or Onlay, escalate the case to Orange County (OC). Yareli clarified that this Inlay/Onlay material/design is handled as EMAX for routing purposes, so it should not be processed as a normal single-unit Zirconia Crown case.
Keywords: Zirconia Mono, Zirconia Monolithic, single unit, Inlay, Onlay, EMAX, OC, Orange County, valid escalation, escalate
Notes: Historical clarification: Rosemarie's case that had been tagged Invalid Escalation should be corrected to Valid Escalation because the case was submitted at approximately 12:10 AM and Yareli's clarification was provided later at approximately 2:08 AM. This was an FYI/process clarification, not a team callout.
Purpose: Define routing for single-unit Zirconia Monolithic Inlay/Onlay cases and prevent them from being treated as standard Ninja Zirconia Crown cases.
Step-by-Step Procedure:
1. Review the Rx restoration/design and material before proceeding with normal ABS entry.
2. If the case is a single-unit Zirconia Monolithic Inlay or Onlay, do not process it as a standard single-unit Zirconia Crown.
3. Escalate the case to Orange County (OC).
4. Treat the escalation as valid because the Inlay/Onlay material/design is handled as EMAX for this routing rule.
5. Document the case disposition according to the current approved OC escalation workflow.
Stop / Escalate When: Escalate every single-unit Zirconia Monolithic Inlay/Onlay case to OC. If the restoration type or material wording is unclear, stop and verify rather than assuming it is a normal Zirconia Crown.
